meaning: [authors: "two phases"] progressive lipofuscin accumulation to 24 months, then qualitatively new inclusions (PHF-like, Hirano bodies) from 24 months
[authors: "abrupt telomere shortening"] model: gradual shortening plus stochastic abrupt events explain bimodal clonal senescence
in vitro ageing: diploid to tetraploid until growth crisis, then hypotetraploid immortalised cells
[authors: "terminal decline", "developmental cascade"] distinct paths: age-related vs dementia-related vs mortality-related; cascade from low memory to dementia to death (longitudinal)
[authors: "stepwise"] replicating -> reversible quiescence -> irreversible senescence states with distinct miRNA profiles
[authors: "terminal decline or drop"] terminal drop in cognition weaker in centenarians (longitudinal)
[authors: "three stable post-developmental states", "transition"] machine-classified morphological states; isogenic same-age worms in state I vs II are molecularly distinct
[authors: "punctuated equilibrium"] individual health histories show stasis punctuated by sudden changes; growth-curve models build in an assumption of gradual change by aggregating individuals
[authors: "waves of hematopoiesis", "transcriptional age states"] distinct HSC states across gestation, maturation and aging, incl. a fetal-specific state
[authors: "stable fixed points", "aging trajectories"] gene-circuit feedback; destabilisation of homeostatic loops accelerates aging (yeast SIR2-HAP circuit)
